shape.text: Vercel's changelog names the stem vci for integration tokens and prints no value.
It is not established that an integration token is vci_ followed by 56 characters, as the sibling classes with provider examples are.

unresolved.reason: No Vercel page, specification or source writes vci_ with the underscore or shows a value; the underscore, 56-character body and alphabet come from scanner rules only, from three owners but one source class.

shape.text: Kingfisher, Betterleaks and secretlint have rules for the class. Kingfisher's and Betterleaks's examples are synthetic values; Betterleaks copies Kingfisher's examples; secretlint accepts 20 to 60 letters and digits. GitHub's vercel_integration_access_token type names the class and not a shape.

issuance.text: Integration tokens are obtained by creating an integration and running the OAuth code exchange.

unresolved.reason: Whether OAuth code exchange now returns vci_ tokens is undocumented; the Building Integrations page still shows unprefixed 24-character access-token and client values in its examples, which look legacy or stale.

issuance.text: None of the shape properties has been checked against an issued token.

unresolved.reason: No integration token was issued for this research; the planned check (marker with underscore, total length 60, body alphabet and whether the last 6 characters checksum the previous 50) was not performed.

openQuestions.text: Do the five classes share one generator, so that the structure of vcp_ and vca_ extends to vci_?

unresolved.reason: No source says whether the five classes share one generator.
